title: How does GPS work when satellites are so far away?
sources: Einstein's Theory of General Relativity in GPS

lines.text: GPS satellites orbit twelve thousand miles above Earth, yet guide you to a restaurant doorway.
Each satellite simply broadcasts a radio message saying: this is who I am, and this is the exact time.
Because radio waves travel at the speed of light, your phone calculates how long the signal took to arrive.
lines.caps: Your phone measures *nanosecond | delays in the | *signal

lines.text: Multiply that time by light speed, and your phone knows its exact distance from the satellite.
Here is the crazy part: because satellites move fast in weaker gravity, their clocks tick faster than Earth clocks.
lines.caps: Satellite clocks tick *faster | due to Einstein's | *relativity!

lines.text: Engineers must program Einstein's theory of general relativity into GPS software every day, or navigation would fail by six miles.
lines.caps: Without relativity, *maps | would fail by | *6 miles!

lines.text: Every GPS turn you make is living proof that Einstein was right.
